skill_name: Compare and contrast the two types of philosophical ethics - deontological and utilitarian.
workflow: Deontological ethics, or duty-based ethics, emphasizes adherence to a set of universal moral standards and principles, regardless of the consequences. Utilitarian ethics, or consequence-based ethics, emphasizes actions that will produce the greatest good for the greatest number of people. However, both approaches recognize that moral decision making involves an inherent risk of harm and uncertainty.
